consensus_summary: The new moon is the lunar marker beginning Israel’s month and sacred calendar, associated with recurring worship and renewal and, in Christian typology, treated as a ceremonial shadow fulfilled in Christ. The blind responses generally do not make a particular visible lunar phase central.
book_summary: The book likewise identifies the new moon as the phase beginning the month and marking appointed times, but specifically identifies it as the full moon associated with the east gate, rejecting the commonly taught conjunction or first-visible-crescent identification.
consensus_core_identification: The lunar month-opening marker and its associated appointed observance.
book_core_identification: The full moon as the lunar month-opening marker, linked with the east gate and appointed times.
boundary_disagreement: The book retains the consensus category of a lunar phase marking the month’s beginning but reclassifies which phase qualifies: it includes the full moon and excludes the conjunction or first visible crescent recognized by the common view.
material_contradiction: There is a material contradiction at the phase boundary: the full moon and the conjunction/first crescent cannot both be the uniquely identified beginning phase of the same lunar month under the same calendrical scheme. This does not replace the broader shared category of a month-opening lunar observance.
rationale: The minimum cores overlap in identifying the new moon as the lunar marker for the beginning of the month and an appointed worship time. The book’s distinctive claim concerns the precise astronomical phase, so it materially revises the extension of that shared category rather than replacing the category altogether. The east-gate association adds specificity but does not itself create a different central referent.
strongest_objection: The printed texts support a recurring month-opening observance, appointed worship, and the opening of Ezekiel’s east-facing gate on the new-moon day, but none explicitly states that the new moon is the full moon or that Israel’s month began at the full moon. Ezekiel’s east gate is architectural and does not by itself identify a lunar phase.
